source_evidence.anchor: Exercise 2.2.3 (Bounding the hyperbolic cosine): displayed inequality followed by `for all x ∈ R`
source_evidence.observation: The exercise asks to show exactly `cosh(x) ≤ exp(x²/2)` for every real x.

source_evidence.anchor: Hint: Compare the Taylor’s expansions of both sides.
source_evidence.observation: This sentence is a proof hint; it does not add a hypothesis, conclusion, or equality claim to the requested result.

binders: x ∈ R, universally quantified by the phrase `for all x ∈ R` (PDF page 5; printed page 16, Exercise 2.2.3 displayed inequality).
conclusions: cosh(x) ≤ exp(x²/2) (PDF page 5; printed page 16, Exercise 2.2.3 displayed inequality).
definitions_and_conventions: The selected passage uses `cosh` for the hyperbolic cosine and `exp` for the exponential in the displayed inequality, without giving separate local definitions (PDF page 5; printed page 16, exercise title and displayed inequality).
The exponent on the right-hand side is exactly x²/2, with coefficient 1/2 (PDF page 5; printed page 16, Exercise 2.2.3 displayed inequality).

details: The claim is universal over all real x, with no exceptional cases or side conditions (PDF page 5; printed page 16, anchor `for all x ∈ R`).
The comparison is non-strict and bounds cosh(x) above by exp(x²/2): `cosh(x) ≤ exp(x²/2)` (PDF page 5; printed page 16, displayed inequality).
The exponential argument is x squared divided by 2; the constant is exactly 1/2 (PDF page 5; printed page 16, displayed inequality `exp(x²/2)`).

The instruction to compare Taylor expansions is proof guidance only and is not part of the proposition to be shown (PDF page 5; printed page 16, anchor `Hint: Compare the Taylor’s expansions of both sides.`).

undebatable_constraints: The quantified domain is all real numbers x, not a restricted subset (PDF page 5; printed page 16, anchor `for all x ∈ R`).
The inequality direction and relation are exactly `cosh(x) ≤ exp(x²/2)` (PDF page 5; printed page 16, displayed inequality).
The exponent is exactly x²/2, preserving the square and the constant 1/2 (PDF page 5; printed page 16, displayed inequality).
There are no stated hypotheses beyond x being real (PDF page 5; printed page 16, complete Exercise 2.2.3 statement).
The Taylor-expansion sentence is a hint and must not be promoted to a premise or conclusion (PDF page 5; printed page 16, sentence labeled `Hint`).
contract_plain_english: For every real number x, prove that the hyperbolic cosine of x is at most the exponential of x squared divided by 2. The suggestion to compare Taylor expansions is only a proof hint, not part of the claim (PDF page 5; printed page 16, Exercise 2.2.3 and its labeled hint).
